reason: E2 shows that a CrTaO4 layer reduced oxidation in a different alloy (NV1), but that alloy has a distinct composition (Al, Cr, Mo, Nb, Ti, Si) and the mechanism relied on reduced Ti content, not simply Cr addition. E1 shows Cr addition to WVTaTi promoted Laves phase precipitation and improved oxidation resistance, but this is a different alloy system (W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr) on a steel substrate, not equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr. Neither study provides evidence that a ~5 at.% Cr addition to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will form a protective CrTaO4 scale or preserve mechanical properties.
premises: Cr addition promotes formation of a protective CrTaO4-based scale in refractory alloys
A CrTaO4 layer reduces oxidation in a multi-principal-element refractory alloy
Minor Cr addition (~5 at.%) will not significantly degrade room-temperature ductility or high-temperature strength of HfNbTaTiZr
